papers.title_en: TI-StegoAlign: Channel-Guided Post-Training for Generative Text Steganography under Tokenization Inconsistency
papers.authors: Jiuan Zhou, Yuhao Xue, Yu Cheng, Yuan Xie, Zhaoxia Yin
papers.evidence: 面向分词不一致的稳健文本信息嵌入，与鲁棒水印技术相关。
papers.tldr: 生成式文本隐写依赖发送端和接收端共享令牌状态，但实际接收端仅见表面文本，重新分词导致令牌边界改变、状态失同步，现有评估高估恢复率。提出TI-StegoAlign后训练框架，用BCSO扩大发送端嵌入位置的编码边际，用CCPO以接收端真实恢复、文本质量与反隐写分析为反馈，优化完整隐写文本。接收端比特准确率达100%，困惑度偏差降低21.6%，反隐写分析性能相对提升6.3%。仅更新LoRA参数，无需通信时特殊修正，实现接收端可靠的高精度隐写，为通道感知的生成式隐写提供新范式。
papers.abstract_en: Generative text steganography enables LLM agents to exchange secret information through task-relevant messages. Yet most methods evaluate recovery on sender-side tokens, whereas the receiver observes only surface text. Detokenization and receiver-side retokenization can alter token boundaries, desynchronize coding states, and cause such evaluation to overestimate receiver-side recovery. Existing remedies rely on inference-time filtering or verification, correcting individual outputs without adapting the generation policy to the receiver-side channel. To address these limitations, we propose TI-StegoAlign, a channel-guided post-training framework. The Bit-Consistent Supervised Objective (BCSO) enlarges local coding margins at realized sender-side embedding positions. Channel-Conditioned Preference Optimization (CCPO) then aligns complete stegotexts using receiver-realistic recovery, text quality, and anti-steganalysis feedback. TI-StegoAlign updates only LoRA parameters and requires no tokenization-specific correction during communication. Experimental results show 100% receiver bit accuracy. Compared with the strongest baselines, TI-StegoAlign achieves a 21.6% reduction in normalized perplexity deviation and a 6.3% relative improvement in anti-steganalysis performance.
